title.narrative: Strengthening local stakeholders’ early-warning and early-response System to ethno-religious divide

description.narrative: Plateau State has gone through recurrent ethno-religious clashes since 2001 leading to hundreds of casualties and IDPs. Bordering Southern Kaduna LGAs have also been strongly affected. Since then, civil society (including youth and women organizations), religious umbrella organizations and the State authorities have joined forces to attend humanitarian needs, and create concertation frameworks to avoid violent relapses. In Plateau State, the LGAs of Barkin Ladi, Mangu and Bokkos are particularly concerned as shown by the 2023 Black Christmas and 2024 January and February attacks that caused more than 850 killings, and 15.000 IDPs (UNICEF, 2024). These events confirm the notorious increase of the IDP number in the State that had been stabilized since 2020 (OIM, 2024). The situation in Southern Kaduna (Kaura, Zangon Kataf & Jema’a) has also drawn attention with deadly attacks on ethno-religious lines on a regular basis. Kafanchan and the surroundings LGAs are then areas with the highest number of IDPs in the State (OIM, 2024). This project will build the local capacities to implement a Barometer of cultural and religious pluralism tailored to the local context of Nigeria, and provide the local change actors (public and civil society stakeholder) with an updated and precise overview of the identity-driven stakes in the target areas to implement appropriate social cohesion responses and set up a framework with local change actors to improve coordination, co-construction and monitoring on peacebuilding in Plateau and Kaduna States while fostering an advocacy channel on addressing ethno-religious divides from the local, to the State, Federal and Regional levels, out of the results of the Barometer experiment
